issues.title: [Epic · Week 6] Controlled preview, lowiro authorization, approved data integration, and release activation
issues.outcome: Deploy a controlled synthetic preview, obtain and record lowiro's decision, integrate only the approved data scope, then activate public release through explicit QA and human sign-off.
scope: Separate technical deployment from public publication.
Own authorization, data integration, audits, rollback, and activation order.
acceptanceCriteria: Synthetic preview can exist without being represented as an Arcaea release.
Authorization decision is recorded.
Only approved data/media enter the release candidate.
Final activation has reproducible evidence and rollback.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 6 · Preview] Deploy a controlled synthetic preview and test rollback
issues.outcome: Deploy the production build with synthetic records for maintainer/stakeholder review without activating an Arcaea-specific public release.
scope: Pinned least-privilege deployment, environment protection where available, synthetic banner, noindex controls, base-path/direct-link smoke tests, artifact inventory, and rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: Deployment is reproducible.
Only synthetic data and approved placeholders are present.
Preview is clearly labeled and non-indexed.
Direct links/assets work.
Rollback is tested or dry-run evidenced.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 6 · Legal] Submit prototype package and obtain lowiro publication/data authorization
issues.outcome: Present the mature synthetic prototype and exact publication proposal to lowiro, then record the written decision and permitted scope without treating silence as approval.
scope: Prepare private/controlled preview, screenshots, route inventory, proposed data fields, source plan, branding, hosting, monetization status, excluded content, security/privacy posture, correction/takedown flow, and rollback.

Ask separately about project naming, factual metadata, prose summaries, official links, APIs/files/database access, media, attribution, caching, transformation, and open-source repository publication.
Retain raw correspondence privately and commit only a redacted decision summary with evidence hash when appropriate.
Translate every condition, expiration, revocation, and attribution requirement into implementation/release controls.
nonGoals: Do not request credentials, proprietary bundles, encryption keys, or unrestricted internal access.
Do not publish private correspondence or personal contact data.
acceptanceCriteria: The request describes an implemented prototype rather than an abstract idea.
The proposed data and media scope is field-level and route-level specific.
A written response, rejection, or explicit unresolved status is recorded.
No response is explicitly treated as no authorization.
Approved and prohibited scopes are machine/actionable for `content-update`, `release-content-audit`, and `public-release-activation`.
evidence: Permission request package and reviewed screenshots.
Redacted decision summary or explicit no-response/rejection record.
Maintainer approval of the interpreted permitted scope.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 6 · Data] Integrate the permission-approved Arcaea data source and build release snapshots
issues.outcome: Replace the synthetic adapter with a reviewed Arcaea source adapter only within the exact lowiro-approved scope, while preserving deterministic validation and rollback.
scope: Map the approved API, file export, repository, or database source behind the existing catalog adapter.
Record source applicability, field transformations, attribution, caching, retention, and update cadence.
Generate normalized records, indexes, catalog diffs, snapshots, and changelog.
Keep synthetic fixtures for tests and preserve the last-good release snapshot.
Reject any unapproved field, asset, endpoint, extraction method, or community bulk dataset.
acceptanceCriteria: The integration uses only the recorded approved source and scope.
No UI route requires direct access to the upstream database/API.
Schema, duplicate, reference, source, permission, size, and generated-output checks pass.
Added/changed/removed/unknown records are reviewable.
Rollback to the synthetic preview or prior approved snapshot is documented and tested.
If authorization does not include data access, the issue remains blocked or is replanned without inventing a source.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 6 · Release] Final catalog accuracy, source, asset, and editorial audit
issues.outcome: Audit the exact permission-approved catalog and media artifacts proposed for release.
scope: Freeze candidate versions/counts, verify source links, approval scope, attribution, prose originality, unknowns, alt text, relationships, and no synthetic placeholder is presented as official.
acceptanceCriteria: Every released asset and data category is inside approved scope.
High-impact facts have source records.
No placeholder is represented as official.
Report identifies reviewer, commit, versions, counts, exceptions, and rollback target.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 6 · Community] Contribution guide, issue forms, content review, and maintainer boundaries
issues.outcome: Prepare contribution paths that preserve the approved source, data, asset, and publication boundaries.
scope: Correction/bug/accessibility/feature forms, approved-data review checklist, private-evidence guidance, Code of Conduct, response expectations, and AI disclosure.
acceptanceCriteria: Contributors can submit corrections without repository-wide knowledge.
Forms never request proprietary files or private evidence publicly.
Asset/data submissions require approved basis.
Maintainer capacity and boundaries are honest.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 6 · QA] Release-candidate acceptance, regression, and readiness gate
issues.outcome: Verify the exact approved-data release candidate and produce a transparent go/no-go report.
scope: Routes/content, keyboard/contrast/responsive/offline/SEO/performance/security/legal checks, broken links, permission audit, known issues, and rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: All P0 flows pass.
No unapproved data or asset is present.
Exceptions are documented and approved.
Readiness report links reproducible evidence.
QA does not itself activate public release.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.

issues.title: [Week 6 · Release] Approve and activate the Arcaea-specific public release
issues.outcome: Make the final human go/no-go decision and activate public indexing/promotion only when authorization, data integration, audit, QA, deployment, and rollback evidence are complete.
scope: Review the written lowiro scope and every implementation condition.
Verify the exact release commit, catalog version, asset manifest, deployment host, disclaimer, contact path, robots/sitemap state, and rollback target.
Enable public metadata, indexing, sitemap, canonical host, and release communication only after approval.
Record no-go reasons and keep the synthetic preview or private build when any blocker remains.
acceptanceCriteria: Authorization is valid for the exact project, host, name, data, media, and distribution mode.
The approved-data integration, final audit, and release QA are complete.
The release candidate contains no out-of-scope data or media.
Correction/takedown and rollback paths are operational.
Maintainer records an explicit go/no-go decision.
A no-go leaves the project in a safe synthetic/private state.
evidence: Maintainer go/no-go comment tied to immutable commit/catalog/asset versions.
definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria are verified.
Relevant documentation and tests are updated.
No unreviewed legal, accessibility, security, performance, privacy, or publication exception is introduced.
